subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

choices: She go to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She going to school every day.
She is go to school every day.

solution.correct_choice: She goes to school every day.

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Present Simple - for habits and routines.

📖 THE RULE:
With he/she/it → add -s or -es to the verb!

✏️ HOW IT WORKS:
I go → She goes
   ↑        ↑
  (no s)   (+s)

🎁 SIGNAL WORDS:
'every day' = routine = Present Simple

💡 REMEMBER:
I/you/we/they → go
he/she/it → goes

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'She go' (missing -s)
• 'She is go' (wrong structure)
• 'She going' (missing 'is' for continuous)

✅ Answer: She goes to school every day.

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

choices: Look! The cat sleep on the sofa.
Look! The cat sleeps on the sofa.
Look! The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
Look! The cat slept on the sofa.

solution.correct_choice: Look! The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Present Continuous - for actions happening RIGHT NOW.

📖 THE RULE:
'Look!' = something is happening NOW
→ Use Present Continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing

✏️ STRUCTURE:
[am/is/are] + [verb + ing]
The cat is sleeping
      ↑     ↑
     is   -ing

🎁 SIGNAL WORDS:
Look! Listen! Right now! At the moment!
→ Present Continuous!

💡 COMPARISON:
• Every day → Present Simple (habit)
• Right now → Present Continuous (now)

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
Using Present Simple for current actions!

✅ Answer: Look! The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence for yesterday.

choices: I am walking to school yesterday.

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Past Simple - for completed actions in the past.

📖 THE RULE:
'yesterday' = past = Past Simple

✏️ HOW TO FORM:
Regular verbs: add -ed
walk → walked
play → played

🎁 SIGNAL WORDS:
yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020
→ Past Simple!

💡 REMEMBER:
Past Simple is the SAME for all persons:
I walked, you walked, he walked, we walked

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'I walk yesterday' (wrong tense)
• 'I was walked' (wrong structure)

✅ Answer: I walked to school yesterday.

subject: EN
prompt: Yesterday I ___ my homework and ___ TV.
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Past Simple with irregular verb (do → did).

📖 IRREGULAR VERBS:
Some verbs don't add -ed!
do → did (NOT 'doed'!)
see → saw
go → went

✏️ REGULAR vs IRREGULAR:
• watch → watched (regular: +ed)
• do → did (irregular: changes completely)

💡 COMMON IRREGULAR VERBS:
do → did
go → went
see → saw
have → had
make → made
get → got

⚠️ IMPORTANT:
You MUST memorize irregular verbs!

✅ Answer: did / watched

subject: EN
prompt: Which signal word indicates Present Simple?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Signal words help you choose the right tense!

📖 SIGNAL WORD GUIDE:

✏️ PRESENT SIMPLE (habits):
• every day/week/Monday
• always, usually, often
• sometimes, never

🎁 PRESENT CONTINUOUS (now):
• right now
• at the moment
• Look! Listen!

💡 PAST SIMPLE (finished):
• yesterday
• last week/year
• ago
• in 2020

⚠️ TRICK:
'every...' = routine = Present Simple

✅ Answer: every Monday

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'She ___ (not/like) pizza.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Present Simple negative with he/she/it.

📖 THE RULE:
he/she/it → doesn't + base verb
(NOT 'don't'!)

✏️ STRUCTURE:
[doesn't] + [verb (no s!)]
She doesn't like
     ↑         ↑
  doesn't   no 's'!

🎁 FULL PATTERN:
I/you/we/they don't like
he/she/it doesn't like

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'She don't like' (wrong helper)
• 'She doesn't likes' (double s!)

💡 REMEMBER:
The 's' goes to 'doesn't', NOT to the verb!

✅ Answer: doesn't like

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct question.
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Yes/No questions in Present Simple.

📖 THE RULE:
[Do/Does] + [subject] + [base verb]?

✏️ STRUCTURE:
Do you like pizza?
↓   ↓    ↓
Do  you  like (base form!)

🎁 WHEN TO USE WHICH:
• I/you/we/they → DO you like?
• he/she/it → DOES she like?

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'Like you pizza?' (missing Do)
• 'Does you like?' (wrong match: Does + you)
• 'Do you likes?' (verb shouldn't have -s)

💡 WORD ORDER:
Statement: You like pizza.
Question: Do you like pizza?

✅ Answer: Do you like pizza?

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct question.
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Questions with he/she/it in Present Simple.

📖 THE RULE:
he/she/it → DOES + base verb (no -s!)

✏️ STRUCTURE:
Does she like coffee?
  ↓    ↓    ↓
Does  she  like (NOT likes!)

🎁 REMEMBER:
The 's' is already in 'Does'!
Does + like (NOT likes)

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'Does she likes?' (double -s!)
• 'Do she like?' (wrong: Do + she)

💡 COMPARISON:
Statement: She likes coffee.
Question: Does she like coffee?
          ↑ The 's' moved to 'Does'!

✅ Answer: Does she like coffee?

subject: EN
prompt: Make a question: 'You went to Berlin.' → '___?'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Past Simple questions.

📖 THE RULE:
[Did] + [subject] + [base verb]?

✏️ STRUCTURE:
Did you go to Berlin?
 ↓   ↓   ↓
Did  you  go (BASE form, not 'went'!)

🎁 IMPORTANT:
'Did' already shows past tense!
The main verb goes back to BASE form:
went → go

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'Did you went?' (double past!)
• 'Do you went?' (wrong tense)

💡 COMPARISON:
Statement: You went to Berlin.
Question: Did you go to Berlin?
               ↑ Back to base form!

✅ Answer: Did you go to Berlin?

subject: EN
prompt: Complete the short answer: 'Do you speak English?' - 'Yes, ___.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Short answers in English.

📖 THE RULE:
Answer with the SAME helper verb!

✏️ PATTERN:
Do you...? → Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Does she...? → Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
Did they...? → Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.

🎁 WHY SHORT ANSWERS?
In English, just 'Yes/No' sounds incomplete!
'Yes' is okay, but 'Yes, I do' is better.

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'Yes, I speak' (not wrong, but not natural)
• 'Yes, I am' (wrong helper verb)

💡 REMEMBER:
The helper verb in the question = helper verb in answer!

✅ Answer: I do

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the best option: 'You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a bike.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Modal verbs - 'must' for rules and obligations.

📖 MODAL MEANINGS:
• can = ability (Ich kann...)
• must = obligation/rule (Ich muss...)
• should = advice (Ich sollte...)
• might = possibility (vielleicht)

✏️ CONTEXT:
Helmet when riding = safety RULE
→ must (you HAVE to!)

🎁 STRUCTURE:
Modal verbs + BASE VERB (no 'to'!)
You must wear (NOT 'to wear')

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'You must to wear' (no 'to' needed!)
• Using 'can' for rules (can = ability, not rule)

💡 REMEMBER:
Modals never change: he must, she must, they must (NOT 'musts'!)

✅ Answer: must

subject: EN
prompt: '___ you help me with my homework?'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Modal verbs - 'can' for requests and ability.

📖 'CAN' USES:
1. Ability: I can swim. (Ich kann schwimmen.)
2. Permission: Can I go? (Darf ich gehen?)
3. Request: Can you help? (Kannst du helfen?)

✏️ HERE:
Asking for help = polite request
→ Can you help me?

🎁 COMPARISON:
• Can you...? = friendly request
• Must you...? = not natural for requests
• Could you...? = more formal/polite

⚠️ DON'T CONFUSE:
'Can' (Können) ≠ 'Must' (Müssen)

✅ Answer: Can

subject: EN
prompt: 'You ___ eat more vegetables. It's good for your health.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Modal verbs - 'should' for advice.

📖 'SHOULD' = Advice (Ratschlag)
It's a GOOD IDEA, but not a strict rule.

✏️ CONTEXT:
'good for your health' = advice, recommendation
→ should (you SHOULD do this)

🎁 COMPARISON:
• must = you HAVE to (Pflicht)
• should = it's a good idea (Empfehlung)
• can = you are able to (Fähigkeit)

💡 GERMAN TRANSLATION:
should ≈ sollte
must ≈ muss

⚠️ NOTE:
'Should' is softer than 'must'!

✅ Answer: should

subject: EN
prompt: Match the words with the meaning.

right: a place to wait for a train
pairs: a place to wait for a train
a place to wait for a train

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Travel vocabulary - essential words for journeys.

📖 THE WORDS:

✏️ TICKET
= Fahrkarte, Eintrittskarte
a paper or digital pass to travel or enter

🎁 LUGGAGE
= Gepäck
bags and suitcases you take on a trip

💡 PLATFORM
= Bahnsteig
the place at a train station where you wait

⚠️ PRONUNCIATION:
• luggage = /ˈlʌɡɪdʒ/
• platform = /ˈplætfɔːm/

✅ Matches:
ticket → a paper or digital pass
luggage → bags and suitcases
platform → a place to wait for a train

subject: EN
prompt: What does 'departure' mean?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Travel vocabulary - departure vs arrival.

📖 THE WORDS:

✏️ DEPARTURE (Abfahrt/Abflug)
= when you LEAVE
• departure time = Abfahrtszeit
• departure gate = Abflug-Gate

🎁 ARRIVAL (Ankunft)
= when you ARRIVE
• arrival time = Ankunftszeit

💡 MEMORY TRICK:
• DEpart = leave (DE- like 'weg-')
• ARrive = come (like 'ankommen')

⚠️ AT AIRPORTS:
Departures = where you check in to LEAVE
Arrivals = where people COME from flights

✅ Answer: when you leave

subject: EN
prompt: What is a 'timetable'?

choices: a schedule showing when lessons happen

solution.correct_choice: a schedule showing when lessons happen

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
School vocabulary.

📖 TIMETABLE (Stundenplan)
= a schedule showing when lessons/events happen

✏️ EXAMPLE:
Monday 8:00 - Math
Monday 9:00 - English
→ This is a timetable!

🎁 RELATED WORDS:
• schedule = Zeitplan
• lesson = Unterrichtsstunde
• subject = Schulfach
• break = Pause

💡 ALSO USED FOR:
• bus timetable = Busfahrplan
• train timetable = Zugfahrplan

✅ Answer: a schedule showing when lessons happen

subject: EN
prompt: Which word means 'Frühstück'?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Daily life vocabulary - meals.

📖 MEALS OF THE DAY:

✏️ BREAKFAST (Frühstück)
= the FIRST meal of the day (morning)
break + fast = 'breaking the fast' from sleeping

🎁 LUNCH (Mittagessen)
= midday meal (around 12:00)

💡 DINNER (Abendessen)
= evening meal (around 18:00-20:00)

⚠️ SNACK (Snack/Zwischenmahlzeit)
= small food between meals

💡 MEMORY TRICK:
Break-FAST = first meal, you 'break' your 'fast' (not eating while sleeping)

✅ Answer: breakfast

subject: EN
prompt: Read: 'Tom missed the bus, so he arrived late. The teacher was not angry because Tom had a note from his mother.' What is true?

choices: Tom arrived late and had an excuse.

solution.correct_choice: Tom arrived late and had an excuse.

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Reading comprehension - finding facts in a text.

📖 TEXT ANALYSIS:
'Tom missed the bus' → He was late
'arrived late' → confirms he was late
'not angry because Tom had a note' → he had an excuse

✏️ CHECK EACH ANSWER:
• 'arrived early' → FALSE (text says 'late')
• 'arrived late and had an excuse' → TRUE ✓
• 'teacher was angry' → FALSE (text says 'not angry')
• 'missed the train' → FALSE (text says 'bus')

💡 READING TIP:
Look for EXACT words in the text!
'bus' ≠ 'train'
'not angry' ≠ 'angry'

✅ Answer: Tom arrived late and had an excuse.

subject: EN
prompt: Read: 'Dear Lisa, I can't come to your party on Saturday. I have to visit my grandmother. Sorry! Love, Anna.' Why can't Anna come?

choices: She has to visit her grandmother.

solution.correct_choice: She has to visit her grandmother.

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Reading comprehension - understanding a message.

📖 TEXT ANALYSIS:
'I can't come to your party'
'I have to visit my grandmother'
→ The reason is clearly stated!

✏️ READING STRATEGY:
Find the REASON:
'I can't come' = what she can't do
'I have to...' = why (the reason)

🎁 TEXT TYPE:
This is a short MESSAGE (informal note).
• 'Dear Lisa' = greeting
• 'Love, Anna' = closing

💡 TIP:
In short texts, the answer is usually directly stated!

✅ Answer: She has to visit her grandmother.

subject: EN
prompt: Read: 'Subject: Meeting tomorrow. Hi team, the meeting is at 10 a.m. in Room 5. Please bring your notes. Best, Mr. Smith.' When is the meeting?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Reading emails - finding specific information.

📖 EMAIL STRUCTURE:
• Subject line: 'Meeting tomorrow'
• Greeting: 'Hi team'
• Body: time, place, request
• Closing: 'Best, Mr. Smith'

✏️ FINDING INFORMATION:
Time: 'at 10 a.m.'
Place: 'in Room 5'
Request: 'Please bring your notes'

🎁 EMAIL READING TIP:
Scan for KEY WORDS:
• Numbers (10, 5)
• Time words (a.m., p.m.)
• Place words (Room, office)

💡 CAREFUL:
'Room 5' is the PLACE, not the time!

✅ Answer: 10 a.m.

subject: EN
prompt: Fix the sentence: 'He dont like football.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Error correction - Present Simple negative.

📖 THE ERROR:
'He dont like' → TWO mistakes!
1. 'dont' should be 'doesn't' (he/she/it)
2. Missing apostrophe

✏️ CORRECT FORM:
he/she/it + doesn't + base verb
He doesn't like
     ↑         ↑
  doesn't   no -s!

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'doesn't likes' → double marking!
• 'don't' with he/she/it → wrong helper
• 'not like' → missing helper verb

💡 RULE:
The -s goes to 'doesn't', NOT the main verb!

✅ Answer: He doesn't like football.

subject: EN
prompt: Fix the sentence: 'Yesterday I go to the cinema.'

choices: Yesterday I goes to the cinema.
Yesterday I went to the cinema.
Yesterday I am go to the cinema.
Yesterday I going to the cinema.

solution.correct_choice: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Error correction - Past Simple.

📖 THE ERROR:
'Yesterday' = past time
'go' = present form
→ Tense mismatch!

✏️ CORRECTION:
go → went (irregular verb!)

🎁 IRREGULAR VERB:
go - went - gone
NOT: go - goed - goed!

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• Using present tense with past time words
• 'goed' (go is irregular!)

💡 SIGNAL WORD CHECK:
Yesterday = PAST → use PAST tense!

✅ Answer: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

subject: EN
prompt: Fix the sentence: 'She can to swim very well.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Error correction - Modal verbs.

📖 THE ERROR:
'can to swim' → 'to' is wrong!
Modal verbs DON'T use 'to'!

✏️ CORRECT STRUCTURE:
[modal] + [base verb] (NO 'to'!)
She can swim
    ↑    ↑
  can  swim (not 'to swim')

🎁 MODAL VERBS:
can, must, should, will, would, might
→ ALL followed by BASE VERB, no 'to'!

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'can to swim' → remove 'to'
• 'cans swim' → modals don't add -s!
• 'can swims' → base verb, no -s!

✅ Answer: She can swim very well.

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'My name ___ Lisa.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
The verb 'to be' - basic introduction.

📖 'BE' FORMS:
• I am
• you are
• he/she/it is
• we are
• they are

✏️ HERE:
'My name' = it (a thing)
→ My name IS Lisa

🎁 COMMON PHRASES:
• My name is...
• I am... years old
• I am from...

💡 SHORTCUT:
If it's not I/you/we/they, use 'is'!

⚠️ DON'T SAY:
'My name am Lisa' ✗
'My name are Lisa' ✗

✅ Answer: is

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'A car is ___ than a bike.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Comparatives - comparing two things.

📖 THE RULE:
Short adjectives (1-2 syllables) → add -er
fast → faster
tall → taller

✏️ STRUCTURE:
[adjective + er] + than
A car is faster than a bike.

🎁 SPELLING RULES:
• fast → faster
• big → bigger (double consonant)
• happy → happier (y → i)

⚠️ LONG ADJECTIVES:
3+ syllables → more + adjective
• beautiful → more beautiful
• NOT 'beautifuler'!

💡 REMEMBER:
Comparing TWO things = -er or 'more'
Superlative (THE best) = -est or 'most'

✅ Answer: faster

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'This is the ___ book I have ever read.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Superlative + irregular adjective.

📖 'THE ___' = SUPERLATIVE
Comparing more than 2 → superlative (the -est)

✏️ IRREGULAR FORMS:
good → better → best
bad → worse → worst
many → more → most

🎁 STRUCTURE:
the + superlative
'the best book'

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES:
• 'the most good' ✗ (good is irregular!)
• 'the better' ✗ (that's comparative)
• 'more good' ✗ (irregular!)

💡 MEMORIZE:
good - better - best
bad - worse - worst

✅ Answer: best

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense is used for habits and regular actions? Example: 'I usually watch TV in the evening.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Identifying the Simple Present tense.

📖 SIMPLE PRESENT - USES:
• Habits and routines (Gewohnheiten)
• General facts (Fakten)
• Regular actions (regelmäßige Handlungen)

✏️ FORMATION:
Infinitive (+ -s/-es for he/she/it)
I watch → He watches

💡 SIGNAL WORDS:
• usually, sometimes, always
• every day, often, never
• on Mondays, in the morning

🎁 EXAMPLES:
• I usually watch TV. (Gewohnheit)
• The sun rises in the east. (Fakt)
• She works in Berlin. (regelmäßig)

⚠️ NOT:
• Present Progressive = NOW (gerade jetzt)
• Present Perfect = connection past-present

✅ Answer: Simple Present

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense is correct? 'I have just arrived at the airport.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Identifying the Present Perfect tense.

📖 PRESENT PERFECT - USES:
• Action just completed (gerade abgeschlossen)
• Past action with present result
• Experience (Erfahrung)

✏️ FORMATION:
have/has + past participle (3rd form)

✏️ ANALYSIS:
'I HAVE just ARRIVED'
  ↓           ↓
have    +  past participle
= PRESENT PERFECT

💡 SIGNAL WORDS:
• just, recently (gerade)
• yet, already, still
• since, for
• ever, never

🎁 EXAMPLES:
• I have just finished. (gerade fertig)
• She has lived here since 2010. (seit)
• Have you ever been to London? (jemals)

✅ Answer: Present Perfect

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense is correct? 'They are calling their grandma right now.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Identifying the Present Progressive tense.

📖 PRESENT PROGRESSIVE - USES:
• Action happening NOW (jetzt gerade)
• Temporary situation
• Fixed plans (feste Pläne)

✏️ FORMATION:
to be (am/is/are) + verb + -ing

✏️ ANALYSIS:
'They ARE CALLING their grandma right now.'
      ↓    ↓
   are + calling (-ing)
= PRESENT PROGRESSIVE

💡 SIGNAL WORDS:
• right now, now
• at the moment
• currently
• Look! Listen!

🎁 EXAMPLES:
• I am studying right now. (gerade jetzt)
• She is working at the moment. (im Moment)
• Look! It is raining! (Schau!)

⚠️ NOT Simple Present:
'They call' = habit/regularly
'They are calling' = right now

✅ Answer: Present Progressive

subject: EN
prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form: 'She ___ (go) to school every day.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Simple Present with he/she/it.

📖 THE RULE:
Simple Present + he/she/it → add -s or -es

✏️ WHY 'GOES'?
1. 'every day' = Signal for Simple Present ✓
2. 'She' = 3rd person singular
3. go → goes (add -es)

💡 SPELLING RULES FOR -S/-ES:
• Most verbs: add -s (play → plays)
• Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: add -es
  go → goes
  watch → watches
  wash → washes
• Verbs ending in consonant + y: y → ies
  study → studies
  try → tries

⚠️ NOT:
• 'is going' = Present Progressive (NOW)
• 'has gone' = Present Perfect

✅ Answer: goes

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past form of 'go'?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Irregular verb: go - went - gone

📖 IRREGULAR VERBS:
They don't follow the regular -ed pattern!
You must memorize them.

✏️ GO (irregular verb):
Simple Present: go/goes
Simple Past: went
Past Participle: gone

💡 USAGE:
• 'I went to school yesterday.' (Simple Past)
• 'I have gone home.' (Present Perfect)

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
'goed' is WRONG! ❌
'go' is irregular → 'went'

🎁 MORE IRREGULAR VERBS:
• see → saw → seen
• come → came → come
• take → took → taken
• write → wrote → written

✅ Answer: went

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'write'?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Irregular verb: write - wrote - written

📖 THE THREE FORMS:
1. Infinitive/Simple Present: write
2. Simple Past: wrote
3. Past Participle: written

✏️ WHEN DO WE USE PAST PARTICIPLE?
• Present Perfect: I have written a letter.
• Past Perfect: I had written a letter.
• Passive: The letter was written.

💡 SIMILAR PATTERN (-en ending):
• write → wrote → written
• drive → drove → driven
• ride → rode → ridden
• rise → rose → risen

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
'writed' is WRONG! ❌
Irregular verbs don't use -ed!

✅ Answer: written

subject: EN
prompt: Match the verbs with their Simple Past forms.
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Irregular verbs - Simple Past forms.

📖 THE MATCHES:
• see → saw (sehen → sah)
• take → took (nehmen → nahm)
• know → knew (wissen → wusste)
• tell → told (erzählen → erzählte)

💡 FULL FORMS:
• see - saw - seen
• take - took - taken
• know - knew - known
• tell - told - told

🎁 LEARNING TIP:
Learn verbs in groups with similar patterns!

Group 1 (same Past & Participle):
tell → told → told
sell → sold → sold
send → sent → sent

Group 2 (vowel change):
see → saw → seen
know → knew → known

✅ All pairs matched correctly!

subject: EN
prompt: Which sentence uses the Present Perfect correctly?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Correct use of Present Perfect with 'since'.

📖 THE RULE:
SINCE + point in time → PRESENT PERFECT
FOR + duration → PRESENT PERFECT

✏️ ANALYSIS:
✓ 'I have lived here since 2020.'
  Present Perfect + since = CORRECT!

❌ 'I have lived here yesterday.'
  yesterday = finished time → Simple Past needed!

❌ 'I lived here since 2020.'
  since = needs Present Perfect!

❌ 'I am living here since 2020.'
  since = needs Present Perfect, not Progressive!

💡 SINCE vs. FOR:
• SINCE + point: since 2020, since Monday, since 3pm
• FOR + duration: for 5 years, for 2 hours, for a week

🎁 EXAMPLES:
• I have worked here since January.
• I have worked here for 6 months.

✅ Answer: I have lived here since 2020.

subject: EN
prompt: Which is the correct question form? 'She likes pizza.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Forming questions in Simple Present.

📖 THE RULE:
Do/Does + subject + infinitive (without -s)?

✏️ FORMATION:
Statement: She likes pizza.
Question: Does she like pizza?

💡 DO vs. DOES:
• DO for I, you, we, they
• DOES for he, she, it

⚠️ IMPORTANT:
When using DOES, the main verb loses the -s!
• She likes → Does she like? ✓
• NOT: Does she likes? ❌

🎁 MORE EXAMPLES:
• He plays tennis. → Does he play tennis?
• They work here. → Do they work here?
• You speak German. → Do you speak German?

❌ WRONG FORMS:
• 'Do she like?' - wrong helper
• 'Is she like?' - 'be' only for be-verbs/progressive
• 'Like she?' - missing do/does

✅ Answer: Does she like pizza?

subject: EN
prompt: Which is the correct negative form? 'I like spinach.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Forming negations in Simple Present.

📖 THE RULE:
Subject + do/does + not + infinitive

✏️ FORMATION:
Positive: I like spinach.
Negative: I do not like spinach.
Short form: I don't like spinach.

💡 DON'T vs. DOESN'T:
• DON'T (do not) for I, you, we, they
• DOESN'T (does not) for he, she, it

🎁 EXAMPLES:
• I don't like spinach. (I)
• She doesn't like spinach. (she)
• They don't work here. (they)
• He doesn't play tennis. (he)

❌ WRONG FORMS:
• 'I doesn't like' - wrong helper for 'I'
• 'I not like' - missing do/does
• 'I no like' - 'no' is not for verbs

⚠️ SHORT FORMS:
• do not = don't
• does not = doesn't

✅ Answer: I don't like spinach.

subject: EN
prompt: Which modal verb expresses ABILITY (Fähigkeit)?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Modal verbs and their meanings.

📖 CAN = ABILITY (Fähigkeit/Können)

✏️ EXAMPLES:
• I can swim. (Ich kann schwimmen.)
• She can speak German. (Sie kann Deutsch sprechen.)
• Can you help me? (Kannst du mir helfen?)

💡 OVERVIEW OF MODALS:
• CAN = ability, possibility (können)
• MUST = obligation, necessity (müssen)
• SHOULD = advice, recommendation (sollte)
• MAY = permission, possibility (dürfen, könnte)

🎁 MORE EXAMPLES:
• You must wear a seatbelt. (Pflicht)
• You should study more. (Rat)
• May I go to the toilet? (Erlaubnis)

⚠️ GRAMMAR RULE:
Modal + infinitive WITHOUT 'to'!
• I can swim. ✓
• I can to swim. ❌

✅ Answer: can

subject: EN
prompt: What is the comparative form of 'big'?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Comparative adjectives - comparing two things.

📖 THE RULE FOR SHORT ADJECTIVES:
Adjective + -er

✏️ FORMATION:
big → bigger

⚠️ SPELLING RULE:
Short adjective ending in consonant-vowel-consonant:
Double the last consonant!
big → bigger (not biger!)
hot → hotter
thin → thinner

💡 MORE SHORT ADJECTIVES:
• small → smaller
• tall → taller
• fast → faster
• old → older

🎁 LONG ADJECTIVES (3+ syllables):
Use 'more' + adjective
• beautiful → more beautiful
• interesting → more interesting

❌ WRONG FORMS:
• 'more big' - big is short, use -er
• 'biger' - need to double the g
• 'biggest' - that's superlative (best of all)

✅ Answer: bigger

subject: EN
prompt: Match the English words with their German translations.
explanation:

School vocabulary (Schulvokabeln).

📖 THE MATCHES:

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'speak'?
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Irregular verb: speak - spoke - spoken

📖 THE THREE FORMS:
1. Infinitive: speak
2. Simple Past: spoke
3. Past Participle: spoken

✏️ USAGE:
• Simple Past: I spoke to him yesterday.
• Present Perfect: I have spoken to him.
• Passive: English is spoken here.

💡 SIMILAR PATTERN:
• speak → spoke → spoken
• break → broke → broken
• steal → stole → stolen
• choose → chose → chosen

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
'speaked' is WRONG! ❌
'speak' is irregular!

🎁 TIP:
Many verbs with 'ea' follow this pattern:
ea → o → o (with -en)

✅ Answer: spoken

subject: EN
prompt: Find the error: 'She don't like coffee.'
explanation:
🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
Error correction - do/does in negations.

📖 THE RULE:
• DON'T for I, you, we, they
• DOESN'T for he, she, it

✏️ THE ERROR:
'She don't like coffee.' ❌
'She' = 3rd person singular → needs DOESN'T

✏️ CORRECT SENTENCE:
'She doesn't like coffee.' ✓

💡 WHY NOT 'LIKES'?
After doesn't, use the infinitive (base form)!
• She doesn't like ✓
• She doesn't likes ❌

🎁 MORE EXAMPLES:
• He doesn't work here. ✓
• It doesn't matter. ✓
• They don't know. ✓
• I don't understand. ✓

⚠️ COMMON MSA MISTAKE:
Mixing up don't/doesn't is very common!
Remember: he/she/it → DOESN'T

✅ Answer: don't should be doesn't

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense? 'I usually watch TV in the evening.'
explanation:
🎯 SIMPLE PRESENT

📖 USE:
For habits and regular actions.

✏️ SIGNAL WORDS:
• usually, always, often
• every day, sometimes
• never

💡 EXAMPLE:
'I USUALLY watch TV'
→ 'usually' = habit/regular action
→ Simple Present!

📐 FORMATION:
Infinitive (+ -s/-es for he/she/it)

✅ Answer: Simple Present

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense? 'They are calling their grandma right now.'
explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PROGRESSIVE

📖 USE:
For actions happening RIGHT NOW.

✏️ SIGNAL WORDS:
• right now, now
• at the moment
• Look! Listen!

💡 EXAMPLE:
'They ARE CALLING right now'
→ Action is happening NOW
→ Present Progressive!

📐 FORMATION:
am/is/are + verb + -ing

✅ Answer: Present Progressive

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense? 'He has lived here since 2003.'
explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PERFECT

📖 USE:
Action started in the past and continues to the present.

✏️ SIGNAL WORDS:
• since, for
• already, yet
• just, recently
• ever, never

💡 EXAMPLE:
'He HAS LIVED here SINCE 2003'
→ Started in 2003, still living there now
→ Present Perfect!

📐 FORMATION:
have/has + past participle

✅ Answer: Present Perfect

subject: EN
prompt: Fill in the correct form: 'I ___ just ___ at the airport.' (arrive - Present Perfect)
explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PERFECT FORMATION

📐 RULE:
have/has + past participle

✏️ HERE:
• Subject 'I' → use 'have' (not 'has')
• 'arrive' → past participle: 'arrived'

💡 'JUST' = very recently
→ Typical Present Perfect signal word!

✅ Answer: I HAVE just ARRIVED at the airport.

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past of 'go'?
explanation:

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: go

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'write'?

💡 USE:
• Simple Past: She WROTE a letter yesterday.

write - wrote - written
(all different!)

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past of 'see'?
explanation:

'seed' is a noun (Samen)!
'sawed' is from 'saw' (sägen)!

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'speak'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: SPEAK

speak - spoke - spoken
(like break - broke - broken)

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past AND Past Participle of 'put'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: PUT

• Simple Present: put

put - put - put

📖 SIMILAR VERBS:
• cut - cut - cut

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence:

choices: She has already finished her homework.
She have already finished her homework.
She has already finish her homework.
She already has finished her homework.

solution.correct_choice: She has already finished her homework.

explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PERFECT - WORD ORDER

📐 STRUCTURE:
Subject + have/has + (already/just/never) + past participle

✏️ ANALYSIS:
• 'She' (3rd person) → 'has' (not 'have')
• 'finish' → past participle: 'finished'
• 'already' comes AFTER have/has

⚠️ WRONG:
• 'She have...' (wrong auxiliary)
• 'She has finish...' (missing -ed)
• 'She already has...' (wrong word order)

✅ Answer: She has already finished her homework.

subject: EN
prompt: Which signal word indicates Present Perfect?
explanation:

📖 PRESENT PERFECT:
• since, for
• already, yet
• just, recently
• ever, never
• so far, up to now

📖 SIMPLE PAST:
• yesterday
• last week/month/year
• ago

📖 SIMPLE PRESENT:
• every day, always
• usually, often

📖 PRESENT PROGRESSIVE:
• now, at the moment

✅ Answer: since (Present Perfect)

subject: EN
prompt: Which modal verb expresses OBLIGATION? 'You ___ wear a seatbelt.'
explanation:
🎯 MODAL VERBS: OBLIGATION

📖 MUST:
Expresses strong obligation/necessity.
'You MUST wear a seatbelt' = It's required!

📖 COMPARISON:

• should = advice
• can = ability/permission

'must' is often used for rules and laws.

subject: EN
prompt: Which modal verb expresses ABILITY? 'She ___ speak three languages.'
explanation:

Expresses ability (what someone is able to do).

'She CAN speak three languages'
= She is able to speak them.

📖 COMPARISON:
• can = ability NOW
• could = ability in the PAST
• will be able to = ability in FUTURE

✅ Answer: can

subject: EN
prompt: What is the comparative of 'good'?
explanation:

'gooder' and 'more good' do NOT exist!

• bad - worse - worst

subject: EN
prompt: What is the superlative of 'beautiful'?

Adjectives with 3+ syllables:

• beautiful
• more beautiful

'beautifuler' is WRONG!

prompt: What does 'to spend money' mean in German?

spend - spent - spent

subject: EN
prompt: What does 'to lose' mean in German?
explanation:

lose - lost - lost

subject: EN
prompt: A sign says: 'Zeb throws objects. Please beware - his aim is accurate.' What does this mean?

Look for KEY WORDS to understand the meaning!

subject: EN
prompt: Which question is correct?
explanation:
🎯 QUESTIONS IN SIMPLE PRESENT

📐 RULE:
Do/Does + subject + infinitive (WITHOUT -s)?

✏️ ANALYSIS:
• 'she' (3rd person) → use 'Does'
• After 'Does' → infinitive WITHOUT -s!
• 'like' (not 'likes'!)

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
'Does she likes...' is WRONG!
The -s is already in 'Does'!

✅ Answer: Does she like pizza?

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past of 'think'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: THINK

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: think
• Simple Past: THOUGHT
• Past Participle: thought

• think - thought - thought
